correctness.rationale: Graph automorphisms permute equal-sized part classes, making π(x)_i=sum_{v in V_i}x_v and σ(y)_v=y_i/n_i equivariant. Their linear interpolation preserves the set of occupied parts, so gives an honest strong deformation retraction simultaneously for every t, including t>r when the target is a full simplex. A geometric H-fixed barycentric point has equal part coordinates on each H-part orbit; a selection of orbits occupies sum of weights parts, giving strict quota <t. When no orbit weight<t the fixed realization is empty; otherwise choose a least admissible weight w0. Decompose quota as B ∪ (Q0*A). All faces of B\A have weights in [t-w0,t), and removing any vertex (weight >=w0) puts their entire boundary in A. Collapsing cone(Q0*A) yields one sphere of dimension |S|-1 for each qualifying subset, including dimension zero and empty conventions; integral homology is free. The finite verification checks are not used for the all-part proof.
